criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (coral reef/ocean monitoring with fluid lensing), rationale (bleaching, acidification), single spacecraft justification, and users/operators (CSIRO/BOM, Australian University/Gov) all clearly addressed with discussion and references.

evidence.quote: Earth observation satellite – specifically for coral reef and ocean monitoring
only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity
would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All space segment elements covered: launch vehicle/site with justification, SSO LEO characteristics with Keplerian elements and STK 3D views, maneuvers (direct injection + EOL deorbit), ground facility with access summary and ground tracks, duration 5 years and drag-sail EOL. Supported by screenshots and calculations.

evidence.quote: proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport
an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924°
selected – the Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusion synthesizes launch, orbit, ground station and EOL choices from evidence and notes risk (Vega E not yet built, alternative Vega C). Could be more quantitative but clearly appropriate and evidence-based.

evidence.quote: fully described satellite configuration has been constructed. The initial problem of not catching coral bleaching events
A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Report has logical structure and executive summary, generally readable. Figures/tables inconsistently labelled (no Figure numbers/titles), OCR artifacts. Uses Wikipedia as proper source against instruction, and references are bare URLs not properly cited, matching Adequate.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Uses Argument of Latitude for circular orbit instead of undefined arg perigee/true anomaly; acceptable workaround but technically should set ω=0 and specify true longitude; inclination calculation correct.
Extensive use of Wikipedia timeline for launch selection against task guidance not to use Wikipedia as proper source.

overall: Solid coral-reef SSO mission benefiting Australia with well-justified launch, orbit, ground station and EOL using STK. Introduction and design comprehensive. Presentation weakened by informal figure captions and Wikipedia referencing.

feedback.summary: You delivered a solid, well-justified coral-reef SSO mission for Australia. Introduction and main design comprehensively cover launch, orbit, ground station and EOL with STK evidence. Your Vega E from Guiana, 600 km SSO at 97.7924 deg, Mount Pleasant access, and drag-sail EOL are persuasive. Presentation limits your overall mark due to figure labelling and referencing.
next_steps: Add formal Figure numbers, titles and in-text callouts for all STK views (e.g. Image 4 12h-apart view) and access reports, to move presentation to Accomplished.
Replace Wikipedia timeline citations in Launch and Bibliography with proper aerospace sources (ESA, industry) and format references with author/date and proper in-text citation.
In Conclusion, add quantitative summary from your Orbit and Ground Control & Communications results (revisit, coverage %, deorbit delta-v/time) to strengthen evidence-based closure.

criteria.C1: You did well in Introduction: primary mission (fluid-lensing coral/ocean monitoring), rationale (bleaching/acidification), single-satellite justification, and users CSIRO/BOM/university/gov clearly addressed. For Accomplished upper band, add more literature on stakeholder needs and explicit number trade-off.
criteria.C2: Strong coverage: Vega E from Guiana Space Centre, 600 km SSO with 97.7924° inclination calculation, direct injection, Mount Pleasant access, 5-year life and drag-sail EOL – all supported by STK 3D views and reports. To improve, justify inclination source and refine circular-orbit elements (set ω=0, use true longitude).
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion synthesises Launch, Orbit, Ground Control & Communications and EOL from evidence and acknowledges Vega E risk with Vega C alternative. For higher Accomplished, make it more quantitative – summarise key performance numbers from your design.
criteria.C4: Report has logical structure and readable executive summary. To reach Accomplished, use consistent Figure numbering/titles instead of informal captions like 'STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart', and replace bare Wikipedia URLs in Bibliography with properly cited authoritative sources.
